intent: Approve a commit without a change check when only wording changed.

edit.summary:
I proposed four elements in the `authoring` domain. All four were accepted as proposals with 0 issues, and none is confirmed yet. I didn't touch `delivery`.

- **`objects.Commit`**: I added an optional boolean property `wording_only`. I proposed this first because the other three proposals reference it. My first attempt at those three was refused until it existed.
- **`actions.approve_commit`**: It now takes an optional `wording_only` param and records it on the commit. The `checks-pass` precondition now reads `checks_passed == true or wording_only == true`. The action still requires a person, and `not-approved` is unchanged.
- **`actions.record_approval`**: The `approved-only-if-checked` precondition now also accepts `target.wording_only == true`.
- **`invariants.approved-commits-passed-their-checks`**: The check now also allows `wording_only == true`, and the reason text says so.

This lets an approver skip the change check by asserting `wording_only`. Nothing verifies that assertion against the actual change. It also loosens an invariant that was previously unconditional, so the pre-deploy check should look closely at this. I made these changes as written and didn't judge whether they're a good idea.
